subject: Distance : new question about point transect and duration

messages.author: 1c0747786e53db70
messages.subject: Distance : new question about point transect and duration
parts:
Hello,
 
For point transects, I understand that the duration affects the results given by Distance software. In a previous email, you said “the longer the sampling duration the higher the density estimate” and you reminded us “animals movement induces bias in density estimate”.
 
So it seems that depending on the environment, we have to find the "good" duration allowing us to record the maximum of present birds without double counting a same bird. Is that right ? Do you have returns of experience on the most adapted duration for point transects ?
 
Best regards,
Gilles Saulas

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Distance : new question about point transect and duration
parts:
Gilles

The subject of point count duration has a long history.  In principle, sampling animal populations, whether by distance sampling or mark-recapture, takes place instantaneously.  The animals are frozen in place while the observer conducts the sampling.  Of course, this is not the case in reality; the job of the observer is to approximate this situation as closely as possible via field methodology.

I ask that you read the paper by Prof Buckland: 

Buckland, S. T. 2006. Point transect surveys for songbirds: robust methodologies’. The Auk 123 (2): 345–345. https://doi.org/10.1642/0004-8038(2006)123[345:psfsrm]2.0.co;2.

Equally, you can listen to him describe the study that he published in The Auk with this video lecture
https://workshops.distancesampling.org/online-course/syllabus/Chapter3/#case-study-of-point-transects-with-songbirds-the-montrave-study
If you want yet more on the subject,

Matsuoka, S. M., Mahon, C. L., Handel, C. M., Solymos, P., Bayne, E. M., Fontaine, P. C. and Ralph, C. J. 2014. Reviving common standards in point-count surveys for broad inference across studies.  The Condor, 116(4):599-608.  https://doi.org/doi: 10.1650/condor-14-108.1
